A negative tuberculin test can occur with miliary TB or with immunosuppression (notably HIV). [THOUGHT] The patient has 6 months of fever, cough, night sweats, weight loss, diffuse pulmonary infiltrates, hepatomegaly, generalized lymphadenopathy, diffuse crackles, negative TST, negative HIV, and negative sputum AFB — this pattern makes disseminated TB less likely and raises strong concern for lymphoma or disseminated fungal infection (or other granulomatous disease). An excisional lymph‑node biopsy will provide tissue for definitive histopathology and targeted microbiology (AFB and fungal stains/cultures) and is the single most informative next diagnostic step.

[TEST] Excisional biopsy of an accessible enlarged lymph node with histopathology (H&E), AFB (Ziehl–Neelsen) stain, fungal (GMS/PAS) stains, and sending tissue for mycobacterial and fungal cultures.

Other possibilities (lymphoma, disseminated fungal infection) are less likely given the specific choroidal findings. 

[DIAGNOSIS] Miliary (disseminated) tuberculosis.
